balnĕārĭus (bălĭneārĭus , Inscr. Grut. 171, 8), a, um, adj. id.,
I.of or pertaining to a bath (class. for the preced.): “fur,” lurking about baths, Cat. 33, 1 ; cf. the title in Dig. 47, 17: “de furibus balneariis: furtum,” Dig. 1 . 1. § “3: instrumentum,” a bathing implement, ib. 33, 7, 17 : “vapores,” ib. 43, 21, 3, § 6 .—Subst.: balnĕārĭa , ōrum, n. plur., a place for bathing, a bathing-room, bath: “nihil ei restabat praeter balnearia et ambulationem et aviarium,” Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 1, § 1 ; so id. Att. 13, 29, 2; Col. 1, 6, 2; Sen. Q. N. 4, 9; id. Tranq. 9, 7.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
